summary:
Lubusz Voivodeship stands under the national framework of Poland. No voivodeship-level deviation from Polish law or Polish enforcement practice has been identified as material enough to score separately, so a trans visitor to Lubusz Voivodeship is assessed against Polish statute, Polish detention practice and the binding European Court of Human Rights standard.

Detention carries the clearest documented risk. On 13 March 2024 the Association for Legal Intervention reported that a Polish regional court placed a transgender Vietnamese woman, on hormone therapy since 2018, in a guarded centre for male foreign nationals. Polish law bars such placement wherever a stay would threaten a person's life or health, or where the person shows signs of having suffered violence. The Border Guard refused to move or release her despite that bar, and she was freed only after the association applied to the Border Guard Post commander; the case page was updated on 28 March 2024.

The same report documented her history of violence and sexual assault, which indicates that trans women held in these facilities may be exposed both to interrupted medical care and to violence while in custody.

On 11 July 2024 the European Court of Human Rights found that Polish prison authorities violated a trans woman's right to private and family life under Article 8 of the Convention by denying her hormone replacement therapy in Siedlce prison, awarding EUR 8,000 in damages. The Court left the alleged breaches of Articles 3 and 14 undecided, but held that the refusal had no reasonable legal grounds and was disproportionate. The judgment binds Poland as a whole and therefore governs trans healthcare in Polish prisons and detention, including in Lubusz Voivodeship.
tangentialFactors:
The statutory prohibition on placing a person where a stay would threaten life or health did not by itself secure her transfer. What produced release was an application to the Border Guard Post commander lodged by an outside organisation, so reliance on NGO leverage rather than on the operative rule is the practical pattern to expect if detained while in this voivodeship.

The Article 8 ruling binds Poland as a whole, so a trans visitor detained anywhere in the country litigates under the same standard. That standard does not translate into predictable conditions: Poland operates no specialised trans prison section, and placement decisions remain individual and unpredictable.

Both documented failures occurred in custody rather than at the border. Entry itself is not the pressure point in the sourced material; the risk accumulates after a trans foreign national is placed in a guarded centre or prison.
localsOnly:
Polish residents held in custody have a litigable claim on medication. The European Court of Human Rights held the denial of hormone replacement therapy in Siedlce prison to be disproportionate and without reasonable legal grounds, and awarded EUR 8,000; the judgment is available to anyone held in a Polish facility, not only to foreign nationals.

Domestic law already conditions placement in guarded centres and comparable custody on whether a stay would threaten the person's life or health and on whether the person shows signs of having suffered violence. Enforcement of that condition has been recorded as failing until an external application forced a review, which is the resident-facing position of the rule as applied.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether any guarded centre or immigration-detention facility in Lubusz Voivodeship has held a trans detainee, and how this voivodeship's Border Guard units apply the statutory placement bar, is not sourced in the inventory and remains unresolved.

The prison judgment concerned Siedlce prison, which lies outside Lubusz Voivodeship. No voivodeship-specific data on hormone therapy provision in Polish prisons was located, so conditions in facilities used by visitors in this voivodeship are unresolved rather than established.

The detention case report was updated on 28 March 2024 and states the position at that date. Whether the Border Guard's placement practice has since changed has not been re-verified.
